proposed_patch_under_review.keep: final upload and complete shard upload

artifact_count.arithmetic: remove exactly one remote progress artifact per 45 cells: 1037 - 45 = 992

freeze_19_call.effect: snapshot() correctly acknowledges checkpoint 18 using upload_18, then captures new bytes into checkpoint 19 and leaves those checkpoint-19 chunks pending.

finish_call_as_proposed.effect: snapshot() calls acknowledge(directory,state,index-1=19,upload_18). acknowledge() trusts the supplied ID/digest and marks checkpoint 19 included_chunk_names acknowledged, even though upload_18 contains checkpoint 18, not checkpoint 19.

consequences: The same upload_18 ID/digest is recorded as custody for both checkpoint 18 and checkpoint 19.
Chunks first captured in checkpoint 19 are falsely marked remotely acknowledged.
The final checkpoint excludes those falsely acknowledged chunks from included_chunk_names.
The final manifest custody chain is therefore incorrect; terminal-adjacent captured bytes are not preserved by the final progress artifact.

The separately uploaded complete shard may still contain native shard raw, but it does not repair the false progress-artifact custody statement and does not cover every non-shard STREAM such as driver/wrapper streams.

verdict.reason: PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT_* identifies the immediately preceding checkpoint artifact, not merely the most recent successful artifact. Reusing upload_18 while checkpoint 19 exists produces a false acknowledgment.

workflow_changes: Keep freeze_19 unchanged, including its PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT_* binding to upload_18; this correctly acknowledges checkpoint 18.
For finish, omit PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT_ID and PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT_DIGEST entirely (or pass empty values). Do not bind finish to upload_18.
resulting_semantics: finish snapshot index 20 calls acknowledge(index 19, empty, empty), which is a no-op.
Checkpoint-19 chunks remain pending and are included again in the final bundle together with bytes captured after freeze_19.
The state already records upload_18 because freeze_19 acknowledged it, so the final manifest retains truthful prior custody through checkpoint 18.
The final manifest's all_captured_chunks plus included_chunk_names permits reconstruction from acknowledged artifacts through upload_18 plus the final artifact.
No native raw bytes are deleted or rewritten; the complete shard remains separately uploaded.

interruption_window_risk.interval: after local freeze_19 completes and before the final artifact upload successfully completes
interruption_window_risk.truthful_remote_boundary: upload_18 remains the newest remotely acknowledged prefix
interruption_window_risk.locally_only: checkpoint-19 chunks and any later chunks remain only on the runner until final upload
interruption_window_risk.catastrophic_runner_loss: those suffix bytes can be lost if the runner dies before final upload; they must be reported as unknown/lost runner tail, never as zero
interruption_window_risk.complete_shard_note: The always-uploaded shard can mitigate normal step failures if the runner remains alive, but cannot guarantee recovery after catastrophic runner loss and does not justify a false checkpoint acknowledgment.
interruption_window_risk.comparative_risk: One terminal-adjacent remote prefix is removed; evidence freshness on catastrophic loss can regress by at most that checkpoint interval relative to the current workflow.
